title: POST SEARCH (FACEBOOK)
subtitle: Search over billions of posts, where like counts change constantly.
footer: DDIA: Ch 3 inverted index · Ch 6 term-partitioned index · Ch 11 stream indexing   ·   Similar: Top-K videos · Ad click aggregator · Web crawler · Metrics monitoring

items: Build an inverted index (term → post IDs) from the stream of new posts, sharded by term.
Keep two orderings per term, recency and likes, and update like-based ranking only at thresholds or in batches.
Keep hot postings in memory, move old ones to cheaper storage, and cache popular queries.
Search posts by keyword
Sort results by recency or by likes
(Inputs: create posts, like posts)
Search < 500ms
New posts searchable within ~1 minute
Huge write volume (posts and likes)
Read volume ~10k searches/s
~1B posts/day ≈ 12k/s and ~10× that in likes.
Indexing every like individually is far too much write load, so batch it.

GET /search?q&sort=recency|likes&cursor
inverted index: term → post IDs (recency list) and term → ZSET(post_id, like_bucket)
Naive: LIKE '%term%' on the posts table, a full scan at any real scale.

items: Build an inverted index (term → post IDs) from the event stream, sharded by term. New posts are searchable within seconds.
Two orderings: a recency list and a likes-sorted set.
Keep hot postings in memory and move older ones to blob storage; cache popular queries; intersect posting lists for multi-word queries.
Why not just Elasticsearch?
In a real design it is a fine answer; know its sharding (document-partitioned, scatter-gather) and refresh interval.
Likes change constantly?
Threshold or batched updates to the ranking score; exact counts live elsewhere.
Multi-keyword?
Intersect posting lists, smallest first; consider bigram indexes.
Hot term?
Term-partitioned index means one shard per term, so replicate hot terms.
A Postgres LIKE scan, or re-indexing on every like.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
